content: events-cli first-slice scope decisions (user, 2026-07-23), recorded on devague frame events-first-slice after /scope over issues #1 #2 #3: (1) paho-mqtt >=2,<3 becomes a BASE dependency — pip install events-cli carries the publish client, deps=[] posture deliberately given up, because reachy-mini-cli imports the client from the base wheel (#3 amendment); (2) the hand-rolled argparse CLI STAYS — the agentfront App registry is fed from the same core and derives MCP + HTTP only, CLI/registry parity pinned by our own tests; (3) pipelines DEFERRED — this arc ships producer-owned reachy topics only, devague-as-first-consumer decided when the pipeline layer is built; (4) first arc = the #3 unblock slice (envelope core + importable O(1)-enqueue client + stack verbs with 127.0.0.1:1883:1883 compose + nova-stack migration on spark-f8a9 + PyPI release), durable subscriptions and pipelines follow as separate arcs — #1 pipeline acceptance explicitly NOT met by this slice. Also parked (v1, nonblocking): dynsec identity timing waits until remote access is actually needed; anonymous-on-loopback accepted for the slice.

events-cli envelope core (events_cli/core/, landed 2026-07-24 in the first slice) is deliberately STRICTER than CloudEvents, and these choices will surprise producers if not known: (1) unknown top-level wire keys are REJECTED with a did-you-mean hint rather than preserved as CloudEvents extension attributes — extensions belong in data; loud failure was chosen over silent data loss. (2) type must be lowercase dotted (Task.Requested rejected, not normalised) so two event types cannot look identical to a human. (3) source must be an absolute URI with a scheme (bare builder rejected). (4) schemaVersion must be numeric (v1 rejected) and is REQUIRED on the wire even though the Python constructor defaults it — defaulting on parse would make a v2 producer omission read as v1. (5) data is a defensively-copied plain dict, NOT deep-frozen: MappingProxyType would break dataclasses.asdict, deepcopy, pickle and json.dumps, so data is read-only by contract not by enforcement. (6) frozen dataclass without slots=True on purpose — frozen+slots makes unknown-attribute assignment raise a confusing TypeError instead of AttributeError. (7) hash excludes data so envelopes work in sets; equality still compares everything. Event ids are evt_ + 26-char Crockford ULID, sortable to MILLISECOND granularity only — intra-millisecond monotonicity is NOT implemented, which matters before cursors are built on ids in issue #7. Wire names are camelCase, python attrs snake_case, bridged by WIRE_FIELD_NAMES; traceparent stays lowercase per the W3C header spelling.

reachy-mini-cli's EventClient Protocol (issue #3 comment 3) does NOT structurally match the shipped events_cli.EventClient, verified by introspection 2026-07-24: they declare connected/disconnect()/will_set()/set_on_connect(); we ship is_connected (property), close(), will passed ONLY at construction (will=Will(...) or availability_topic=, because paho requires will before connect), and no set_on_connect at all. Their documented fallback for the missing set_on_connect is to edge-detect connected — which is also renamed, so the fallback breaks too. Only publish() matches (ours returns PublishResult instead of None, which is compatible). Their binding constant also guessed the attribute as EventsClient, not EventClient. Because their import is deliberately total (a wrong attribute degrades to a named no-op), EVERY one of these mismatches presents as the bus being quiet rather than as an error. Answered on issue #3 with a mismatch table plus two options: they rename three things, or we add connected/disconnect/will_set/set_on_connect as thin aliases. Their choice was left open — check the issue thread before assuming either. Also told them to prefer literal 127.0.0.1 over localhost (our compose mapping is v4-only; a dual-stack host resolving v6-first would fail to connect).

events-cli history store decision (t5 spike, 2026-07-24): BUILD BESPOKE minimal append-only JSONL in events_cli/history/, overriding the standing do-not-build-a-store-from-scratch constraint (#2, CLAUDE.md) under the both-siblings-fail condition. Decisive structural fact, independently verified twice: data_refinery.store.Envelope has fields id/content/scope/metadata/hash/type ONLY — no sequence, no ordinal, no timestamp — and store.list() accepts only scope/type/backend, with since/offset/limit/after/cursor appearing NOWHERE in the module source. Spec claim c5 requires the cursor to BE a store-assigned monotonic sequence (evt_ ULIDs sort only to millisecond granularity, no intra-ms monotonicity), so a store with no sequence field cannot supply the one field the arc rests on; bounded read-since would degrade to full-scan-and-slice. Secondary measured evidence: FilesBackend.upsert is read-modify-write, O(N) per append / O(N-squared) ingest (0.560 -> 4.199 ms/append across 250 -> 2000 records). eidetic-cli rejected harder: recall is relevance-ranked not temporal, fetches all candidates before slicing, and pulls data-refinery-cli[store] -> pymongo + neo4j transitively while pinned to the 0.6.x line against data-refinery 0.11.0. NOT disqualifying and credited: data-refinery files backend is stdlib-only with dependencies=[], so it would not have broken our dockerless default test selection. Sharp edge found but avoidable: it dedupes on CONTENT HASH, which destroyed a distinct event in testing — ours must dedupe on event id. Correction to a common belief: eidetic consumes data-refinery by DIRECT IN-PROCESS IMPORT, not over a subprocess boundary. Revisit if data_refinery.store grows a sequence plus bounded list(since=,limit=). Full doc: docs/decisions/2026-07-24-history-store-evaluation.md
